watchOuts.title: Zero Article with Abstract & Philosophical Nouns
watchOuts.detail: French 'l’' and Arabic 'al-' tempt you to add 'the' before general concepts ('The psychology helps us understand the human nature'). Drop 'the' for universal truths: 'Psychology helps us understand human nature, particularly the psychology of habit.'

watchOuts.title: Generic Plural Nouns vs. Specific Groups
watchOuts.detail: Avoid saying 'The historians often debate...' when speaking generally about a profession or group. Use a bare plural for general statements: 'Historians often debate how trade routes shaped philosophy.'

watchOuts.title: Timeless Truths & Philosophical Principles
watchOuts.detail: Avoid slipping into Present Continuous ('I am thinking that stoicism is teaching...') when stating enduring ideas. Anchor timeless principles in Present Simple: 'Stoicism teaches that perception shapes our emotional response.'

watchOuts.title: Narrative Present for Vivid Storytelling
watchOuts.detail: Watch third-person '-s' consistency when switching into the historical or narrative present during a story: 'So the traveler arrives at dawn, knocks on the gate, and realizes the city is empty.'

watchOuts.title: Gerund (-ing) vs. Infinitive after Reflective Verbs
watchOuts.detail: French 'de + infinitive' causes slips like 'avoid to rush' or 'suggest to read.' Pair reflective verbs with -ing: 'I enjoy wandering through old quarters without a map' / 'I recommend reading Ibn Khaldun.'

watchOuts.title: Past Simple Anchors vs. Present Perfect Drift
watchOuts.detail: French 'passé composé' ('J'ai visité...') often triggers 'I have visited Fez in 2019.' Whenever a finished time is anchored, lock into Past Simple: 'When I visited Fez in 2019, we spent hours in the library.'

watchOuts.title: 'Actually' vs. 'Currently' & 'Sensible' vs. 'Sensitive'
watchOuts.detail: 'Actually' means 'in fact' (not 'actuellement'), and 'sensible' means 'practical/wise' (not 'emotionally perceptive'). Use 'currently' for time and 'perceptive' for nuance: 'She is remarkably perceptive about group dynamics.'

watchOuts.title: Direct Objects after 'Discuss', 'Emphasize' & 'Approach'
watchOuts.detail: Avoid 'discuss about philosophy' or 'approach to the question'—both take direct objects in English: 'We discussed ethics at length' and 'How you approach a difficult question reveals your assumptions.'

watchOuts.title: Word Stress on Multi-Syllable Reflective Nouns
watchOuts.detail: French final-syllable rhythm can pull stress onto the wrong syllable in 'de-VEL-op-ment', 'PHI-los-o-phy', and 'PSY-chol-o-gy'. Hit the stressed syllable cleanly and soften unstressed vowels: phi-LOS-o-phy, psy-CHOL-o-gy.

watchOuts.title: Aspirated 'H', 'TH' (/θ/ vs. /ð/), and Crisp 'P' vs. 'B'
watchOuts.detail: Give initial 'H' a clear breath ('history, habit, humility' rather than silent French 'h'), keep 'P' aspirated, and place the tongue lightly between teeth for 'thought' (/θ/) vs. 'though' (/ð/).

watchOuts.title: Setting the Scene Before the Insight
watchOuts.detail: Executive habits often jump straight to the abstract conclusion before grounding the listener. Open with sensory detail in Past Simple ('Three years ago, sitting in a quiet courtyard in Cordoba...'), then pivot to the insight.

scenarios.title: A Place That Changed How You See Time
scenarios.prompt: Describe a city, landscape, or historic site you visited that shifted your perspective on pace, ambition, or permanence. Ground it in a specific sensory memory (Past Simple), then explain the principle you took away (Present Simple).

scenarios.title: The Paradox of Choice in Modern Life
scenarios.prompt: A friend argues that having unlimited options always makes people freer and happier. Push back thoughtfully using an example from human psychology or everyday life—pay close attention to zero articles before abstract nouns (freedom, happiness, choice).

scenarios.title: Bridging Classical Wisdom and Modern Habits
scenarios.prompt: Explain a classical concept—such as intentionality (niyyah), hospitality, or self-discipline—to someone unfamiliar with the tradition, connecting it to how people navigate distraction today.

scenarios.title: The Unplanned Detour
scenarios.prompt: Tell a 90-second story about a travel plan or personal assumption that went completely off-script. Focus on smooth transitions between Past Simple background and vivid turning points without rushing the ending.

scenarios.title: What Makes a Conversation Truly Memorable?
scenarios.prompt: Reflect on the difference between exchanging information and having a genuine dialogue. Use reflective verb patterns naturally ('avoid rushing', 'tend to listen', 'worth exploring').

customCards.term: Fix the articles: "The curiosity and the humility are essential in the philosophy."
customCards.definition: "Curiosity and humility are essential in philosophy."
customCards.example: Curiosity drives discovery, whereas certainty often stops it.
customCards.note: Grammar · Articles (77%): Omit 'the' before uncountable abstract nouns used in a general sense.

customCards.term: Complete: "When traveling, I avoid ______ (follow) rigid itineraries."
customCards.definition: "When traveling, I avoid following rigid itineraries."
customCards.example: I always recommend wandering through a neighborhood early in the morning.
customCards.note: Grammar · Verb Patterns (83%): 'Avoid', 'enjoy', 'consider', and 'recommend' take a gerund (-ing), never 'to + verb'.

customCards.term: Choose the tense: "I ______ (read) Al-Ghazali's reflections when I was in university."
customCards.definition: "I read (/rɛd/) Al-Ghazali's reflections when I was in university."
customCards.example: That book stayed with me long after I finished it.
customCards.note: Grammar · Past Simple (83%): A finished past time marker ('when I was in university') requires Past Simple, not Present Perfect.

customCards.term: C1 Upgrade: "It made me think a lot about how people behave."
customCards.definition: "It prompted me to reflect on human nature."
customCards.example: Watching how strangers treated one another prompted me to reflect on civic trust.
customCards.note: Storycraft · Lexical Precision: 'Prompted me to reflect on' replaces 'made me think about' with effortless authority.

customCards.term: C1 Upgrade: "The atmosphere of the old city was very special and peaceful."
customCards.definition: "The old quarter had a deeply contemplative atmosphere."
customCards.example: At dusk, the courtyard takes on a quiet, contemplative stillness.
customCards.note: Storycraft · Descriptive Precision: 'Contemplative' or 'serene' evokes atmosphere far better than 'special and peaceful'.

customCards.definition: Cognitive bias = a systematic pattern in how the brain distorts judgment. Blind spot = a specific area an individual fails to notice.
customCards.example: Confirmation bias is universal, yet each of us has personal blind spots.
customCards.note: Psychology & Philosophy: Pair both terms to contrast universal human tendencies with personal awareness.

customCards.term: Fix tense & pattern: "Psychology is showing that people tend resisting sudden change."
customCards.definition: "Psychology shows that people tend to resist sudden change."
customCards.example: History shows that gradual shifts often outlast abrupt revolutions.
customCards.note: Grammar · Present Simple & Verb Patterns: Use Present Simple ('shows') for general truths, and 'tend + to + infinitive'.

customCards.term: Narrative Pivot: How do you transition from a story back to its deeper meaning?
customCards.definition: "Looking back, what struck me wasn't [X]—it was [Y]."
customCards.example: Looking back, what struck me wasn't the architecture—it was how unhurried everyone seemed.
customCards.note: Storycraft · Narrative Arc: Bridges Past Simple storytelling into a Present Simple philosophical takeaway.
